entries.title: Ex-Blackhawks defenseman Seth Jones isn't exactly welcomed back, has no hard feelings
entries.summary: <p>Defenseman <b>Seth Jones</b> wasn’t exactly welcomed back Sunday to the United Center, where he played his first game since the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> traded him to the Panthers on March 1, 2025. There was no video tribute and no cheers for Jones, who badly wanted out of Chicago when the going got rough.</p><p>The deal has worked out for both sides. The Panthers got a quality player, and the Hawks got a quality goalie in <b>Spencer Knight</b>, who has stabilized the position. The Hawks also got a first-round draft pick, one of three they have in 2027.</p><p>Former Hawks general manager <b>Stan Bowman</b> had big plans for Jones after acquiring him in a draft-day blockbuster in 2021 and signing him to an eight-year, $76 million contract. Jones was supposed to take over for <b>Duncan Keith</b> as the Hawks’ top defenseman. But almost halfway through the contract, his frustration with all the losing became too much.</p><p>Still, Jones said he has ‘‘nothing but love’’ for the organization.</p><p>‘‘Had an experience here for four years,’’ said Jones, who missed the Panthers’ visit to Chicago last season because of a broken collarbone. ‘‘I like where I’m at now, but I wish this organization nothing but the best.</p><p>‘‘It was a good trade for both sides. I’m sure they’ll be very successful in the future when all these picks grow up and get more experience. It was awesome to be back for the first time.’’</p><p>Jones assisted on the Panthers’ second goal, a power-play goal, giving him 11 assists and 12 points for the season, both second on the team. He also logged 24 minutes, 55 seconds of ice time, more than anyone in the game, and put a team-high-tying four shots on goal.</p><p>On the goal, which gave the Panthers a 2-1 lead in the first period, Jones skated into the high slot with the puck and shot it toward the net. It probably would have gone wide, but it deflected in off <b>Matthew Tkachuk</b>.</p><p>‘‘I had so much time, I was kind of shocked,’’ Jones said. ‘‘I was just trying to get it in there. Sometimes you need those.’’</p><h3>Forsling returns, too</h3><p>Jones wasn’t the only former Hawks defenseman on the ice. <b>Gustav Forsling</b>, who played for the team in 2016-19, has turned into a shutdown defenseman for the Panthers, helping them to back-to-back Stanley Cup titles in 2024 and 2025.</p><p>But the Hawks weren’t the only ones who gave up on Forsling. The Canucks drafted him in 2014 and traded him to the Hawks the next year. The Hawks traded him to the Hurricanes, who put him on waivers in 2021. That’s when the Panthers claimed him.</p><p>‘‘Gustav was a late developer,’’ Panthers coach <b>Paul Maurice</b> said. ‘‘He just had to put some size on his frame, and he became so focused on his fitness and his size. He worked himself into being an NHLer. We’re lucky on that one, getting a player like that.’’</p><p>Forsling played 23:12, including a team-high 6:23 short-handed. He helped the Panthers kill all seven Hawks power plays.</p><h3>Notes</h3><p>Having played one of the toughest schedules in the league to start the season, the Hawks finally will face an opponent in their weight class Tuesday, when the Kings come to town. Both teams have six points. It will be the second of back-to-back games for the Kings, who visit the Rangers on Monday.</p><p>• Before the game, the Hawks honored defenseman <b>Ian Cole</b> for playing in 1,000 career games, a milestone he reached Friday. In 17 NHL seasons, he has 233 points (38 goals) and won Stanley Cups with the Penguins in 2016 and ’17.</p>
entries.author: Jeff Agrest

entries.title: Blackhawks' frustrations mount as breakdown leads to third straight loss
entries.summary: <p>Nothing is going right for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>. They certainly haven’t helped themselves much during a frustrating start to the season, but they haven’t been lucky, either.</p><p>Case in point: Ryan Donato. He had five prime scoring chances Sunday against the Panthers and didn’t convert any. Among them, he couldn’t push a sliding puck into an open net in the first period, and his stick broke after he was set up perfectly in the third.</p><p>The Hawks also couldn’t capitalize on Frank Nazar’s partial breakaway or Cole Smith’s breakaway from the red line, both in the third period. And they allowed the winning goal with 2:23 left after a bad change, falling to the Panthers 3-2.</p><p>The player responsible for the screw-up was defenseman Kevin Korchinski, who otherwise played well in his first game back after being scratched for seven in a row.</p><p>After getting a boost from Connor Bedard’s return and winning his first two games back, the Hawks have lost three in a row and have fallen to 3-8. Their schedule has been a gauntlet, and they’ve had their top forward (Bedard) and top defenseman (Bowen Byram) in the lineup for one game. But the promise of last season and the return of Patrick Kane haven’t yielded positive results.</p><p>‘‘There’s going to be frustration; we’re 3-8,’’ Bedard said. ‘‘You’ve got to use that in the next game and try to dig ourselves out. When you play with that edge, you play a little better. If we can do that the rest of the year, that’d be great.’’</p><p>Scoring would help. The Hawks have three goals during their skid. And for all the excitement surrounding Kane, he has one goal and a team-worst minus-13 plus/minus. He’s on the Hawks’ five-forward power-play unit, an experiment that hasn’t exactly worked. Overall, the power play went 0-for-7 against the Panthers.</p><p>‘‘The power play is mirroring our five-on-five game: We can’t score,’’ coach Jeff Blashill said. ‘‘I can’t say that we don’t get any chances; I think we do. Power plays are funny animals. You can get [lousy] power plays and score and good power plays not.</p><p>‘‘We’re just not scoring easy at all, and we have really good players that are going to score goals that are not scoring.’’</p><p>Shooting would help. The Hawks put 21 shots on net, right at their average. And when they did that, good things tended to happen. Ryan Greene opened the scoring with his first goal of the season. Korchinski shot the puck wide, but it went off the boards to Andrew Mangiapane, who passed to Greene in front of the net.</p><p>The Hawks veritably peppered Panthers goalie Akira Schmid with a whopping nine shots in the second period. One went in when Roman Kantserov took a pass from Kane in the right circle and beat Schmid to tie the score at 2.</p><p>The game appeared headed to overtime until the Hawks’ change went bad. Aaron Ekblad sent a pass from the Panthers’ own end to Lars Eller at the Hawks’ blue line. Eller skated in and beat Spencer Knight to his blocker side.</p><p>‘‘He’s going to want the change back,’’ Blashill said of Korchinski. ‘‘But I thought he played solid in that pair with [Sam Rinzel]. Both of them did a lot of good things. It’s unfortunate that he had the tough change.</p><p>‘‘I thought we did a lot of good things through the majority of the game. I thought the last half of the first [period] was the only time I didn’t like us at all. That was the only time I thought we got pushed around. But we came back out in the second. I thought [we] had great pushback in terms of competing. I thought we had great, great compete.’’</p><p>That hasn’t been enough, however.</p>
